PREPLANNING_CONTEXT: {"version":1,"schema_version":2,"epicId":"94ed-f55c-51f5-45f6","generatedAt":"2026-06-02T00:00:00Z","generatedBy":"preplanning","epic":{"title":"Plan-time intent allocation: assign owner_ticket + test_artifact to every end-state intent item before implementation begins","description":"Intent-allocation manifest contract + three-stage emitters + read/validate + a03c validator + opus assistant + e2e.","successCriteria":["sc-1","sc-2","sc-3","sc-4","sc-5","sc-6","sc-7","sc-8","sc-9","sc-10","sc-11"]},"researchFindings":[],"stories":[{"id":"67bd-b0dd-6e56-4fab","title":"As a tooling author, I want a published intent-allocation-manifest contract with a stable intent_id schema and a mint helper, so that every pipeline stage records intent ownership in one format.","description":"## Description
**What**: Publish plugins/dso/docs/contracts/intent-allocation-manifest.md (contract_version=1) defining the per-entry schema and the validator acceptance rule, and ship plugins/dso/scripts/intent-id-mint.sh that mints stable slug-format intent_ids deterministically.
**Why**: This is the walking-skeleton spine. Every emit/read/validate slice and every downstream consumer (d566, 411b, 7f42, 69e8) references this single contract and intent_id format; without it the rest of the epic has nothing to align to.
**Scope**:
- IN: the contract markdown (per-entry schema: intent_id, owner_ticket, test_artifact{path,kind}, deferred, lightweight, shared_infra, confidence, rationale; manifest-level contract_version=1; unknown-field passthrough requirement; validator acceptance rule); the intent-id-mint.sh helper deriving the slug from {epic_id_prefix, item_index, first_5_words_kebab_case} per the `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+){2,5}` regex; documentation of the additive 7f42 fields (source_files, deferred_test) as forward-compatible optional entries.
- OUT: any stage emitter wiring (sc-2/3/4); read/validate tooling (sc-5/6); the a03c hook (sc-7).","priority":0,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":true,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["intent-allocation-manifest.md exists at plugins/dso/docs/contracts/ and documents every per-entry field (intent_id, owner_ticket, test_artifact.path, test_artifact.kind, deferred, lightweight, shared_infra, confidence, rationale) plus manifest-level contract_version=1 ← Satisfies: sc-1","The contract states the validator acceptance rule verbatim: an entry is valid when intent_id matches the slug regex, owner_ticket resolves to a ticket in the epic subtree (or shared_infra is set), and test_artifact kind/path pairing holds ← Satisfies: sc-1","intent-id-mint.sh emits a slug matching `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+){2,5}` derived from {epic_id_prefix, item_index, first_5_words_kebab_case}, and re-running it with the same inputs returns the identical slug ← Satisfies: sc-1","intent-id-mint.sh emits distinct slugs for two items whose first five words differ, confirming the id is not ordinal-derived ← Satisfies: sc-1","Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic in intent-id-mint.sh, including the stability and determinism cases ← Satisfies: sc-1"],"considerations":["[Stability] intent_id MUST be stable across re-runs: the same DoD/item inputs mint the identical slug so a re-decomposition never re-mints a different id for the same item. This is the load-bearing invariant for all downstream merge logic.","[Forward-compat] The contract must mandate unknown-field passthrough so the additive 7f42 fields (source_files, deferred_test) and any future consumer fields survive read/merge round-trips.","[Shell hygiene] intent-id-mint.sh is a new .sh file; set the executable bit (chmod +x) on creation or the test gate silently skips it.","[Scope] The 7f42 additive-field request (ticket comment) is documented here as optional schema, not implemented as behavior; downstream consumers add their own population logic."],"scopeSplitCandidate":false,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":[],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-1"},{"id":"7d52-5c2a-7d5e-45df","title":"As a feature planner running /dso:brainstorm, I want Phase 3 to emit an INTENT_ALLOCATION_BRAINSTORM comment seeding every drafted SC, so that intent allocation begins at epic-creation time.","description":"## Description
**What**: Wire /dso:brainstorm Phase 3 to emit an INTENT_ALLOCATION_BRAINSTORM: JSON ticket comment on the epic, one entry per end-state SC, via ticket-comment-from-file.sh (temp-file write to avoid ARG_MAX).
**Why**: Establishes the first stage of the allocation manifest so the read/merge path has real brainstorm-stage data to consume and preplanning has a seed to reassign from.
**Scope**:
- IN: brainstorm Phase 3 emitter; per-SC entry minted via intent-id-mint.sh with deferred=true and owner_ticket=epic-itself; temp-file write through ticket-comment-from-file.sh.
- OUT: preplanning/impl-plan emitters (sc-3/4); read/validate (sc-5/6); a03c migration backfill (sc-9).","priority":1,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":false,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["A /dso:brainstorm Phase 3 run on a multi-SC epic posts exactly one INTENT_ALLOCATION_BRAINSTORM: comment on that epic containing one entry per drafted end-state SC ← Satisfies: sc-2","Each emitted entry has deferred=true, owner_ticket equal to the epic id, and an intent_id minted by intent-id-mint.sh matching the slug regex ← Satisfies: sc-2","The comment is written through ticket-comment-from-file.sh via a temp file rather than an inline argument, so large epics do not hit ARG_MAX ← Satisfies: sc-2","When this story is complete, re-running /dso:brainstorm Phase 3 on an epic whose Success Criteria text is unchanged re-uses the existing INTENT_ALLOCATION_BRAINSTORM intent_ids rather than minting new ones; a test asserts identical intent_id sets across two consecutive emitter runs on the same SC set ← Satisfies: sc-2","Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic in the brainstorm Phase 3 emitter ← Satisfies: sc-2"],"considerations":["[Stability] Re-running brainstorm on the same SC text must reuse the same intent_id (delegates to draft-1's mint determinism); the emitter must not re-mint fresh ids on re-run.","[ARG_MAX] Always route the comment body through a temp file; inline JSON in a comment argument breaks on large epics."],"scopeSplitCandidate":false,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":["67bd-b0dd-6e56-4fab"],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-2"},{"id":"c94b-f10e-f83b-420b","title":"As a planner running /dso:preplanning, I want an INTENT_ALLOCATION_PREPLANNING comment that reassigns SCs to story DoDs while preserving intent_ids, so that allocation tracks the decomposition.","description":"## Description
**What**: Wire /dso:preplanning to emit an INTENT_ALLOCATION_PREPLANNING: JSON ticket comment on the parent epic (temp-file write). For each story DoD mint a stable intent_id; when reassigning an epic SC to a story, preserve the existing intent_id and set deferred=false. Under --lightweight, still emit the comment and set lightweight=true on unreassigned items (deferred stays true).
**Why**: Carries allocation from epic-level seeds into story-level ownership and introduces the lightweight-placeholder distinction the validator relies on.
**Scope**:
- IN: preplanning emitter; intent_id preservation on reassignment; deferred=false on reassignment; --lightweight lightweight=true behavior on unreassigned items.
- OUT: brainstorm emitter (sc-2); impl-plan emitter (sc-4); validate finding types (sc-6); assistant dispatch (sc-8).","priority":1,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":false,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["A /dso:preplanning run posts one INTENT_ALLOCATION_PREPLANNING: comment on the parent epic with one entry per story DoD, each carrying a slug-regex intent_id ← Satisfies: sc-3","When a story DoD reassigns an epic SC, the emitted entry reuses that SC's existing intent_id and sets deferred=false ← Satisfies: sc-3","A --lightweight run emits the comment and marks each unreassigned item lightweight=true with deferred=true, distinguishing it from a genuine orphan ← Satisfies: sc-3","When this story is complete, the INTENT_ALLOCATION_PREPLANNING comment is written through ticket-comment-from-file.sh via a temp file rather than an inline argument, so large epics do not hit ARG_MAX ← Satisfies: sc-3","Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic in the preplanning emitter, covering reassignment preservation and the --lightweight path ← Satisfies: sc-3"],"considerations":["[Stability] Reassignment MUST preserve the brainstorm-stage intent_id; minting a new id on reassignment would orphan the seed and break stage-precedence merge.","[ARG_MAX] Route the comment body through a temp file via ticket-comment-from-file.sh; inline JSON in a comment argument breaks on large epics.","[Concurrency] Concurrent preplanning worktrees can emit conflicting comments; this story emits append-only and leaves conflict surfacing to read.sh (sc-5) — do not attempt in-emitter conflict resolution."],"scopeSplitCandidate":false,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":["67bd-b0dd-6e56-4fab"],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-3"},{"id":"ed4b-a9a9-32f5-42bf","title":"As an engineer running /dso:implementation-plan, I want an INTENT_ALLOCATION_IMPLPLAN comment mapping task ACs to test artifacts, so that intent ownership reaches the task layer.","description":"## Description
**What**: Wire /dso:implementation-plan to emit an INTENT_ALLOCATION_IMPLPLAN: JSON ticket comment on the parent story (temp-file write). For each task AC mint a stable intent_id; when reassigning a story DoD to a task preserve the intent_id and set deferred=false; populate test_artifact with the task's proposed test path (kind=new) or an existing test path (kind=existing).
**Why**: Completes the three-stage emit chain so the manifest carries ownership all the way to task-level test artifacts, which downstream consumers (411b, 7f42) read.
**Scope**:
- IN: impl-plan emitter on the parent story; intent_id preservation on DoD-to-task reassignment; test_artifact path+kind population.
- OUT: brainstorm/preplanning emitters (sc-2/3); read/validate (sc-5/6).","priority":1,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":false,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["A /dso:implementation-plan run posts one INTENT_ALLOCATION_IMPLPLAN: comment on the parent story with one entry per task AC carrying a slug-regex intent_id ← Satisfies: sc-4","When a task reassigns a story DoD, the emitted entry reuses that DoD's intent_id and sets deferred=false ← Satisfies: sc-4","Each entry populates test_artifact with kind=new and a proposed test path, or kind=existing and a path that exists on disk ← Satisfies: sc-4","When this story is complete, the INTENT_ALLOCATION_IMPLPLAN comment is written through ticket-comment-from-file.sh via a temp file rather than an inline argument, so large stories do not hit ARG_MAX ← Satisfies: sc-4","Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic in the implementation-plan emitter ← Satisfies: sc-4"],"considerations":["[Stability] DoD-to-task reassignment preserves the story-stage intent_id; a fresh mint would break the stage-precedence merge in read.sh.","[ARG_MAX] Route the comment body through a temp file via ticket-comment-from-file.sh; inline JSON in a comment argument breaks on large stories.","[Attribution] kind=existing references a test path that the planner asserts verifies the intent; static checks cannot confirm semantic coverage (known unmitigated edge per epic blue-team)."],"scopeSplitCandidate":false,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":["67bd-b0dd-6e56-4fab"],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-4"},{"id":"bd01-4aed-32e2-49ce","title":"As a downstream consumer, I want intent-allocation-read.sh to merge all stage comments by stable intent_id with deterministic tiebreakers, so that I read one resolved manifest per epic.","description":"## Description
**What**: Ship plugins/dso/scripts/intent-allocation-read.sh <epic-id> that walks the epic subtree, reads all INTENT_ALLOCATION_<STAGE>: comments, and merges by stable intent_id using stage precedence (brainstorm < preplanning < implementation-plan), most-recent-timestamp within stage, and comment-UUID lexical order as the same-timestamp tiebreaker. Surfaces a _conflicts array for equal-stage duplicates and interleaved-stage anomalies, and preserves unknown fields.
**Why**: This is the read half of the walking skeleton; without a deterministic merge, every consumer and the validator would see raw, conflicting comment streams.
**Scope**:
- IN: subtree walk; stage-precedence merge; timestamp and UUID tiebreakers; _conflicts array (equal-stage duplicates + interleaved-stage anomalies); unknown-field passthrough.
- OUT: finding classification (sc-6); a03c hook (sc-7).","priority":1,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":true,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["intent-allocation-read.sh <epic-id> walks the epic subtree and returns one merged entry per stable intent_id across all INTENT_ALLOCATION_<STAGE>: comments ← Satisfies: sc-5","When the same intent_id appears at brainstorm and preplanning stages, the merged entry reflects the preplanning value, confirming stage precedence ← Satisfies: sc-5","When two same-stage comments share a timestamp, the merge selects the entry whose comment UUID sorts first, producing identical output across repeated runs ← Satisfies: sc-5","The _conflicts array lists equal-stage duplicates and interleaved-stage anomalies such as an implementation-plan timestamp predating a later preplanning write ← Satisfies: sc-5","Unknown entry fields present in input comments appear unchanged in the merged output, and unit tests written and passing cover all merge, tiebreaker, and passthrough logic ← Satisfies: sc-5"],"considerations":["[Determinism] The comment-UUID lexical tiebreaker is the only defense against equal-timestamp non-determinism; it must be applied before output is emitted.","[Clock-skew] Interleaved-stage anomalies from worktree clock skew are surfaced in _conflicts, not silently resolved.","[Shell hygiene] intent-allocation-read.sh is a new .sh file; set the executable bit on creation."],"scopeSplitCandidate":false,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":["67bd-b0dd-6e56-4fab"],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-5"},{"id":"6ef7-ed1d-291e-4b5f","title":"As an a03c migration owner, I want the haiku migration to backfill INTENT_ALLOCATION_BRAINSTORM entries for legacy epics, so that pre-94ed brainstorm-complete epics gain a manifest seed.","description":"## Description
**What**: Deliver the three SC9 cross-epic coordination items: (i) extend a03c's haiku migration of brainstorm:complete-tagged epics to also emit INTENT_ALLOCATION_BRAINSTORM with deferred=true entries per end-state-classified item; (ii) post a ticket comment to a03c-d55e-1393-4f27 referencing 94ed-f55c-51f5-45f6 and SC9 documenting the dependency; (iii) amend a03c's epic description via PR to add a sub-bullet under its migration SC referencing the manifest backfill step.
**Why**: Brings legacy brainstorm-complete epics into the manifest so the validator and downstream consumers operate over the full backlog, not only newly-brainstormed epics.
**Scope**:
- IN: the migration-script extension; the coordination ticket comment; the a03c epic-description PR amendment; the 2-SC fixture proving exactly 2 deferred=true entries with valid intent_ids.
- OUT: a03c's base migration mechanics (external blocker owns these).","priority":3,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":false,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["a03c's migration script, run over a fixture epic whose description has 2 end-state SCs, produces exactly 2 INTENT_ALLOCATION_BRAINSTORM entries each with deferred=true and an intent_id matching the SC1 slug regex ← Satisfies: sc-9","A ticket comment is posted on a03c-d55e-1393-4f27 that references 94ed-f55c-51f5-45f6 and SC9 and documents the cross-epic dependency ← Satisfies: sc-9","a03c's epic description gains, via PR, a sub-bullet under its migration SC referencing the manifest backfill step ← Satisfies: sc-9","Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic in the migration backfill extension, including the 2-SC fixture count assertion ← Satisfies: sc-9"],"considerations":["[External blocker] Depends on a03c-d55e owning the haiku migration script this story extends; this is a cross-epic depends_on at the epic level, coordinated via the a03c blocker, not an in-epic story dependency.","[Cross-epic write] Items (ii) and (iii) mutate a03c's ticket and epic description; sequence them so the coordination comment lands before or with the PR amendment.","[Reuse] The backfill must reuse intent-id-mint.sh so backfilled ids are stable and regex-valid."],"scopeSplitCandidate":false,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":["67bd-b0dd-6e56-4fab","7d52-5c2a-7d5e-45df"],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-9"},{"id":"ffe6-260b-530b-4a95","title":"As a sprint orchestrator, I want intent-allocation-validate.sh to classify the merged manifest into the six finding types with a summary mode, so that orphan and conflict hygiene is checkable.","description":"## Description
**What**: Ship plugins/dso/scripts/intent-allocation-validate.sh <epic-id> that consumes the merged manifest from read.sh and emits the six finding types: orphan_intent, unresolved_ambiguity, stale_entry, pending_intent, lightweight_pending, cross_epic_reference. Supports --summary-mode (group by type, count-only) for high-volume epics. Exits 0 when no actionable findings, non-zero with a count when issues are present.
**Why**: Completes the validate half of the walking skeleton and supplies the finding vocabulary the a03c hook (sc-7) and the e2e test (sc-10) consume.
**Scope**:
- IN: the six finding-type classifiers; --summary-mode; exit-code semantics (pending_intent/lightweight_pending classification per spec — pending_intent informational, lightweight_pending actionable).
- OUT: read/merge logic (sc-5, consumed here); a03c hook wiring (sc-7).","priority":2,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":true,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["intent-allocation-validate.sh <epic-id> classifies merged-manifest findings into the six types orphan_intent, unresolved_ambiguity, stale_entry, pending_intent, lightweight_pending, and cross_epic_reference ← Satisfies: sc-6","An intent_id seeded in a comment but with no resolved entry after merge is reported as orphan_intent, and a lightweight=true item is reported as lightweight_pending distinct from orphan_intent ← Satisfies: sc-6","--summary-mode groups findings by type with count-only output ← Satisfies: sc-6","The script exits 0 when only informational pending_intent findings exist and exits non-zero with the finding count when actionable findings are present ← Satisfies: sc-6","Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic, covering each of the six finding types and both exit-code paths ← Satisfies: sc-6"],"considerations":["[Classification] pending_intent (deferred=true) is informational and non-blocking; lightweight_pending (lightweight=true) is actionable. Conflating them re-creates the orphan-vs-placeholder ambiguity this finding type exists to remove.","[Cross-epic] cross_epic_reference fires only when owner_ticket resolves outside the subtree AND shared_infra is unset.","[Shell hygiene] intent-allocation-validate.sh is a new .sh file; set the executable bit on creation."],"scopeSplitCandidate":false,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":["bd01-4aed-32e2-49ce"],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-6"},{"id":"646a-32bc-c2b3-422f","title":"As a completion verifier, I want a manifest-aware validator registered on a03c's end-state-item hook plus a distinct Intent Allocation Findings section, so that allocation warnings surface at closure.","description":"## Description
**What**: Register a manifest-aware default validator with a03c-d55e's pluggable end-state-item-validator hook (contract_version=1). The validator returns {valid:false, severity:"warn", reason:<finding_type>} for orphan_intent / unresolved_ambiguity / cross_epic_reference, {valid:true} for clean entries, ignores pending_intent and lightweight_pending, and falls back to a03c's basic default when the manifest is absent. Update the completion-verifier output template to add a distinct Intent Allocation Findings section.
**Why**: Makes allocation hygiene observable at closure instead of silently passing through; this is where downstream sprint orchestrators see the findings.
**Scope**:
- IN: validator registration on the a03c hook; warn-severity mapping; manifest-absent fallback to a03c basic default; Intent Allocation Findings section in the completion-verifier output template.
- OUT: a03c's own hook implementation (external blocker); the migration backfill (sc-9).","priority":2,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":false,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["The manifest-aware validator is registered with a03c's end-state-item-validator hook and returns severity=warn with the matching reason for orphan_intent, unresolved_ambiguity, and cross_epic_reference findings ← Satisfies: sc-7","The validator returns valid=true for clean entries and produces no finding for pending_intent or lightweight_pending entries ← Satisfies: sc-7","When the manifest is absent for a legacy ticket, the validator falls back to a03c's basic present-and-schema-valid default ← Satisfies: sc-7","The completion-verifier output template renders a distinct Intent Allocation Findings section that lists warn-severity findings separately from general output ← Satisfies: sc-7","An integration test exercises the registered validator against a real a03c hook invocation in a configuration-isolated environment (HOME set to an empty directory, no pre-existing worktrees, no global git config, no pre-set environment variables) and the test passes ← Satisfies: sc-7"],"considerations":["[External blocker] Depends on a03c-d55e providing the pluggable end-state-item-validator hook (contract_version=1, input {item_text, item_source_ticket_id, closure_timestamp}). This is a cross-epic depends_on at the epic level, not an in-epic story dependency; coordinate via the a03c blocker.","[Observability] The Intent Allocation Findings section exists specifically so warn-severity findings are not buried in general verifier output.","[Live-verified] Hook registration is runtime behavior verified against the real a03c hook, hence the environment-isolated integration test."],"scopeSplitCandidate":false,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":["ffe6-260b-530b-4a95"],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-7"},{"id":"9fd1-f253-835f-4706","title":"As a planner, I want an opus-tier intent-allocation-assistant agent that proposes owners and test artifacts with confidence-based routing, so unassigned intents get attribute-grounded suggestions.","description":"## Description
**What**: Ship plugins/dso/agents/intent-allocation-assistant.md (opus-tier) and wire /dso:preplanning and /dso:implementation-plan to dispatch it only when count(unassigned-or-deferred intent items) > 0. The agent takes the full decomposition tree as structured JSON, unassigned items, and existing manifest entries; it outputs per-item {intent_id, proposed_owner_ticket, proposed_test_artifact, rationale referencing specific ticket attributes, confidence}. Confidence routes acceptance: high pre-accepted, low mandatory review, medium per-item flow; a challenge round forces the planner to identify 1-2 least-confident assignments before proceeding.
**Why**: Reduces manual allocation toil while keeping a human gate on low-confidence and challenge-round items.
**Scope**:
- IN: the agent definition; the threshold-gated dispatch in preplanning and implementation-plan; structured decomposition-tree input; confidence-as-routing; rationale-references-specific-attribute requirement; challenge round.
- OUT: the assistant validation fixture (sc-11).","priority":3,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":false,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["intent-allocation-assistant.md exists at plugins/dso/agents/ and declares opus tier, accepting the decomposition tree, unassigned items, and existing manifest entries as structured input ← Satisfies: sc-8","/dso:preplanning and /dso:implementation-plan dispatch the assistant only when the count of unassigned-or-deferred intent items exceeds zero, and skip dispatch when it is zero ← Satisfies: sc-8","Each assistant suggestion includes proposed_owner_ticket, proposed_test_artifact, a confidence tier, and a rationale that cites a specific ticket attribute rather than a generic owner=current-task assignment ← Satisfies: sc-8","High-confidence suggestions are pre-accepted with single-item reject available, low-confidence suggestions require explicit review, and medium-confidence suggestions are presented one at a time for accept/edit/reject before the next ← Satisfies: sc-8","After all suggestions are presented the flow requires the planner to identify 1-2 least-confident assignments as a challenge round before proceeding, and unit tests written and passing cover the threshold-gate and routing logic ← Satisfies: sc-8"],"considerations":["[Adoption] The rationale-must-reference-a-specific-ticket-attribute requirement is the mitigation against the assistant proposing a generic owner=current-task; enforce it in the agent contract.","[Toil] Confidence-as-routing plus the challenge round bound per-item acknowledge fatigue; medium-tier volume remains a residual risk."],"scopeSplitCandidate":true,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":["c94b-f10e-f83b-420b","ed4b-a9a9-32f5-42bf"],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-8"},{"id":"fb58-8657-7ac1-4eef","title":"As a maintainer, I want an assistant-validation fixture that triggers the assistant on a 5-SC/3-story epic and exercises every confidence tier and acknowledge path, so that the routing UX is proven.","description":"## Description
**What**: Add a fixture preplanning dispatch over a 5-SC, 3-story epic that triggers intent-allocation-assistant, and assert the output includes at least one suggestion at each confidence tier (high, medium, low), the challenge round is exercised (planner identifies 1-2 low-confidence items), and the per-item acknowledge log records accept, edit, and reject at least once each.
**Why**: Validates the assistant's confidence-routing and acknowledge flow as a behavior, not just the agent contract.
**Scope**:
- IN: the 5-SC/3-story fixture and assertions on tier coverage, challenge round, and accept/edit/reject acknowledge log.
- OUT: the assistant agent and dispatch wiring (sc-8, consumed here).","priority":4,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":false,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["A fixture preplanning dispatch over a 5-SC, 3-story epic triggers intent-allocation-assistant and the captured output contains at least one suggestion at each of the high, medium, and low confidence tiers ← Satisfies: sc-11","The fixture exercises the challenge round by having the planner identify 1-2 low-confidence assignments before proceeding ← Satisfies: sc-11","The per-item acknowledge log produced by the fixture records the accept, edit, and reject paths at least once each ← Satisfies: sc-11","The assistant-validation fixture runs in a configuration-isolated environment (HOME set to an empty directory, no pre-existing worktrees, no global git config, no pre-set environment variables) and the test passes ← Satisfies: sc-11"],"considerations":["[Live-verified] SC11 asserts a runtime preplanning dispatch triggers the assistant, so the fixture runs in a configuration-isolated environment.","[Coverage] The fixture must be constructed so the assistant genuinely produces all three confidence tiers; hand-curated SC/story scopes that force tier diversity are acceptable."],"scopeSplitCandidate":false,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":["9fd1-f253-835f-4706"],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-11"},{"id":"bc8f-9777-ef02-4f6a","title":"As a maintainer, I want a synthetic end-to-end test covering happy-path, parallel-sprint duplicate detection, and orphan detection, so that the full allocation loop is regression-protected.","description":"## Description
**What**: Add a synthetic end-to-end test exercising three scenarios across the emit/read/validate/verifier path: (a) HAPPY PATH — brainstorm 3-SC epic, preplanning extends and reassigns (deferred=false), impl-plan extends, read.sh returns zero _conflicts, validate.sh returns zero orphan_intent and zero lightweight_pending; (b) PARALLEL-SPRINT DUPLICATE-DETECTION — two dispatches register a test_artifact against the same intent_id, validate.sh surfaces unresolved_ambiguity AND a dedup warning fires (d566 integration or a synthetic stand-in); (c) ORPHAN-DETECTION — 1-SC epic with --lightweight preplanning and no impl-plan stage yields lightweight=true/deferred=true, validate.sh surfaces lightweight_pending, and completion-verifier produces a non-empty Intent Allocation Findings section naming the SC.
**Why**: Proves the stages compose end to end and protects the loop against regression.
**Scope**:
